title: Capability Gap Inventory
body:
Overview

This record belongs to the Universal Capability Gap and Upgrade Planner Database (public edition), a database that identifies the highest-impact missing capabilities and recommends the next improvements, as master coordinator for the R32 collection, promoting only test-gated changes. Capability Gap Inventory covers the following: lists every measured weakness found by the benchmark suite, with its task class and evidence. The record is written as a complete, usable file: it states what the entry is, how it is used, and what its limits are, and it carries a demo program that was genuinely executed at build time, with its output stored beside the code. Benchmark honesty: this database defines part of the fixed test suite for the R32 capability collection. Its target is 99% measured reliability on defined tasks (TARGET, not measured result). The comparative measurement run comes after building and is not claimed anywhere in this round. As master coordinator for the R32 collection, this pair tracks gap analyses and upgrade recommendations, and promotes only changes that pass the test gate.

How it works

The planner inventories measured weaknesses from the benchmark suite, scores each gap by impact, locates the database or generator that could address it, and recommends upgrades in impact order, promoting only changes that pass the test gate. Applied to this record, the method means the following in practice: lists every measured weakness found by the benchmark suite, with its task class and evidence. The record sits at ladder rank simple in the teaching ladder, which runs simple, then compounded, then most complex, so a reader can start from the simpler records and work toward this one.

Worked example

The demo scores capability gaps by impact and prints the highest-impact gap and its recommendation. The demo program prints:

Gap impact scores: [('retrieval', 40), ('verification', 35), ('generation', 30)]
Highest-impact gap: retrieval (40 points)
Recommendation: address retrieval first, test-gated

Use and limits

The planner recommends from measured gaps only. A gap with no measurement is listed as unmeasured, never ranked as high impact, and no upgrade is promoted without a passing gate result. In practice, a reader can use this record to run the same check on their own tasks: follow the method, compare the result with the worked example, and record any difference with its evidence. The record is one of sixteen in this database, and it cross-links to related databases so the reader can continue from here without guessing where to look next.

Record details

Record fields: gap_area: retrieval; impact_score: high; recommended_upgrade: new specialist database; gate_status: awaiting gate run; task_class: retrieval of existing records.
demo_code:
gaps = [('retrieval', 40), ('verification', 35), ('generation', 30)]
top = max(gaps, key=lambda g: g[1])
print('Gap impact scores: ' + str(gaps))
print('Highest-impact gap: ' + top[0] + ' (' + str(top[1]) + ' points)')
print('Recommendation: address ' + top[0] + ' first, test-gated')
demo_output:
Gap impact scores: [('retrieval', 40), ('verification', 35), ('generation', 30)]
Highest-impact gap: retrieval (40 points)
